[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Technical Tutorial: Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting (AAA) in Cyber Security"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting (AAA) form the foundational framework for intelligent network security access control. Understanding and implementing AAA is critical for securing enterprise environments, managing user privileges, and maintaining audit trails."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Understanding the Core Pillars"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Authentication: The process of verifying the identity of a user, device, or system. Examples include passwords, multi-factor authentication (MFA), and digital certificates."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Authorization: The process of determining what an authenticated user is allowed to do. This involves access control lists (ACLs), role-based access control (RBAC), and permission matrices."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Accounting: The process of tracking user activities and network resource consumption. It logs login times, session durations, data transferred, and commands executed for auditing and forensics."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Standard Protocols Supporting AAA"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"RADIUS (Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service) and TACACS+ (Terminal Access Controller Access-Control System Plus) are the industry standard protocols used to implement AAA across network infrastructure devices like routers, switches, and firewalls."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"RADIUS: Combines authentication and authorization, encrypts only the password during transmission, and uses UDP (ports 1812 and 1813)."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"TACACS+: Separates authentication, authorization, and accounting, encrypts the entire packet payload, and uses TCP (port 49)."},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Configuring AAA on a Cisco Router (Example)"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Below is a practical configuration example demonstrating how to set up AAA authentication using a remote TACACS+ server on a Cisco IOS device."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"conf t
aaa new-model
tacacs server SECURE_SERVER
 address ipv4 192.168.1.100
 key SuperSecretKey123
!
aaa authentication login default group tacacs+ local
aaa authorization exec default group tacacs+ if-authenticated
aaa accounting exec default start-stop group tacacs+
line vty 0 4
 login authentication default"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Best Practices for AAA Implementation"},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always configure a local fallback account in case the centralized AAA server becomes unreachable."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for administrative access to reduce the risk of credential compromise."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Regularly review accounting logs and SIEM integration alerts to detect anomalous command execution or unauthorized access attempts."}]
